title: Formatting, Locales and Text
summary: Turning values into text people can read - format specifiers in String.format and formatted, padding and alignment, NumberFormat and DecimalFormat, Locale and why numbers and dates look different around the world, text blocks, Unicode code points and characters outside the basic plane, and comparing text for people with Collator.

cards.q: Why format numbers for a file with `Locale.ROOT`?
cards.a:
So every computer writes the same decimal point and no grouping

Then the file can be read back anywhere. Without a locale, `String.format` uses the computer's default, so a German machine would write `3,50`, which `Double.parseDouble` cannot read back.

`length()` counts UTF-16 code units, and the emoji needs two of them (a surrogate pair)

Most characters fit in one `char`, but emoji and some rare scripts need two; `codePointCount` counts real characters. (In UTF-8 the emoji is four bytes.)

cards.q: Which format prints 3.14 padded with zeros to width 8?
cards.a:
`"%08.2f"`

The `0` flag pads with zeros, 8 is the width, and `.2` gives two decimals: `00003.14`. `"%8.2f"` pads with spaces instead.
